note: DRAFT v1 module checks and final designation exam for the CARSI Indoor Environment Assessment Practitioner course. Original CARSI questions written for Australian and New Zealand conditions; no IICRC standard text reproduced. SME review and sign-off required before seeding.

quizzes.title: CARSI Indoor Environment Assessment Practitioner — Module 1 check

questions.questionText: A tenant asks you whether the air in her bedroom is safe for her toddler. What do you do?
options: Compare readings with a workplace limit
Give a safe or unsafe verdict
Take an air sample for verdict
Describe the building, refer health questions
questions.explanation: An assessment describes the building. Australian public health guidance says mould test results cannot decide whether a health risk exists, so health questions go to a doctor.

questions.questionText: Which order are the four assessment stages recorded in?
options: Observe, measure, interpret, recommend
Measure, observe, recommend, interpret
Recommend, measure, observe, interpret
Interpret, observe, measure, recommend
questions.explanation: Observe, measure, interpret, recommend. Keeping each stage separate lets a reader check your interpretation against what you actually saw and measured.

questions.questionText: Why does a limitation belong in the written report?
options: It transfers liability to the insurer
It makes the report look longer
It shows what was not checked
It replaces the need for readings
questions.explanation: A limitation written down tells every reader what you could not access or measure. Left out, it becomes an argument later about what you missed.

questions.questionText: Unit 4 leaks; Unit 5 next door smells musty. Which is the pathway in the hypothesis?
options: The shared wall cavity and gaps
The body corporate that hired you
The Unit 5 occupant with asthma
The leaking shower mixer, Unit 4
questions.explanation: The source is the leak, the receptor is the Unit 5 occupant, and the pathway is how the problem travels between them: the shared cavity and the gaps into Unit 5.

questions.questionText: Which reading would best rule out the cavity link to Unit 5?
options: Outdoor air humidity is high this week
Unit 5 wall matches its own reference
Unit 5 occupant reports fewer symptoms now
Unit 4 wall reads much wetter today
questions.explanation: If the Unit 5 side of the shared wall reads the same as an unaffected reference in Unit 5, the moisture is not reaching it, which weakens the cavity hypothesis.

questions.questionText: An occupant tells you they have severe asthma. How does that go in your notes?
options: As a reported fact about receptors
As a reason to skip readings
As proof the house is unsafe
As a diagnosis linked to mould
questions.explanation: Record it as a reported fact. It can raise the priority of the work and supports a recommendation to see a doctor, but you do not judge or link symptoms.

quizzes.title: CARSI Indoor Environment Assessment Practitioner — Module 2 check

questions.questionText: Which NCC climate zone is Brisbane in?
options: Zone 2, warm humid summer
Zone 7, cool temperate climate
Zone 8, alpine mountain climate
Zone 5, warm temperate climate
questions.explanation: Brisbane is in NCC climate zone 2. In humid summers, outdoor air meeting air-conditioned surfaces can condense inside walls and behind furniture.

questions.questionText: In a Hobart winter, where does condensation risk usually run?
options: Humid outdoor air onto cooled interiors
Ground moisture up into roof spaces
Bathroom fans out into living rooms
Moist indoor air onto cold surfaces
questions.explanation: Hobart is cool temperate (zone 7). Warm, moist indoor air reaches cold external walls and ceilings, so condensation forms on the inside in winter.

questions.questionText: A bathroom fan exhausts 25 L/s. About how many cubic metres per hour is that?
options: About 250 cubic metres per hour
About 90 cubic metres per hour
About 900 cubic metres per hour
About 25 cubic metres per hour
questions.explanation: 25 L/s × 3,600 s = 90,000 L/h, and 1,000 L is 1 m³, so the fan moves 90 m³/h.

questions.questionText: Room A is 18 °C / 70% RH; room B is 21 °C / 55% RH. Which statement is right?
options: Both hold about 9 g/kg moisture
Room A holds far more moisture
RH alone shows the moisture content
Room B holds far more moisture
questions.explanation: About 9.0 and 8.5 g/kg. RH depends on temperature, so the colder room looks damper while holding almost the same moisture.

questions.questionText: Room air has a dew point of 12.4 °C. A ceiling corner reads 12 °C. What do you expect?
options: A drop in room humidity ratio
No effect at that surface temperature
Higher RH in the room centre
Condensation forms on the cold corner
questions.explanation: A surface at or below the dew point collects condensation. At 12 °C the corner is just below 12.4 °C, so it is effectively at 100% RH.

questions.questionText: Why do you record which equipment was running with each reading?
options: It replaces the outdoor comparison
It proves equipment was tested
Equipment changes the readings directly
Insurers charge for equipment hire
questions.explanation: Dehumidifiers, heaters and air conditioners change temperature and moisture directly. Without the equipment state, readings from different visits cannot be compared.

quizzes.title: CARSI Indoor Environment Assessment Practitioner — Module 3 check

questions.questionText: A note says "wall dry, 15". What is the biggest problem with it?
options: The number fifteen is too low
No reference, instrument, location or time
It should be written in percent
It should use the imperial scale
questions.explanation: A defensible reading needs value, scale, instrument and mode, location and time, against a reference. "15" alone cannot be repeated or compared.

questions.questionText: A thermal camera shows a cool patch on a wall. What do you do next?
options: Ignore it as camera fault
Report the patch as wet
Confirm with a moisture meter
Paint over the cool patch
questions.explanation: Thermal cameras show surface temperature, not moisture. Cool can mean wet, draughty or uninsulated, so confirm with a moisture meter before reporting.

questions.questionText: How are moisture meter readings made comparable?
options: Same material, instrument, mode, reference
Same room, different meters, averaged
Any material, any meter, today
Different materials, same numeric scale
questions.explanation: Meter scales are relative or material-specific. Compare like with like against a reference from an unaffected area of the same material.

questions.questionText: When is indoor CO2 a fair indicator of ventilation?
options: When a gas heater is running
When the room is empty overnight
When no combustion sources are present
When the windows are all open
questions.explanation: The ABCB handbook says CO2 can be relied on as a ventilation indicator only without significant non-breathing sources such as combustion.

questions.questionText: What can an optical particle counter NOT tell you?
options: How many particles were counted
Which size channels were counted
When the sample was collected
What the particles actually are
questions.explanation: It counts particles by size. Dust, smoke, pollen and spores look alike to it, so use it for same-instrument comparisons, not identification.

questions.questionText: A swab gives a high ATP reading. What does that show?
options: A specific germ has been found
Mould is growing on the surface
The surface is unsafe to touch
Organic residue is on the surface
questions.explanation: ATP devices measure all cellular ATP, so they are a general cleanliness measure. They cannot tell types of organic material apart and are not a mould test.

quizzes.title: CARSI Indoor Environment Assessment Practitioner — Module 4 check

questions.questionText: Mould is clearly visible behind a wardrobe. A buyer wants "a mould test". What is your view?
options: Testing is required before any repair
Testing is generally not considered necessary
Testing will identify the health risk
Testing will prove it is safe
questions.explanation: enHealth says testing is generally not considered necessary where mould is visible, and results cannot decide health risk. Find the moisture source instead.

questions.questionText: When is a sample justified?
options: Whenever the client asks for one
When an occupant reports any symptoms
When it answers a written question
Whenever mould is visible somewhere inside
questions.explanation: Sample only to answer a written question a sample can actually answer, such as hidden growth or a before-and-after comparison of a defined area.

questions.questionText: A pump runs at 15 L/min for 5 minutes. What volume was sampled?
options: 0.075 cubic metres of air
7.5 cubic metres of air
0.75 cubic metres of air
75 cubic metres of air
questions.explanation: 15 × 5 = 75 L, and 75 ÷ 1,000 = 0.075 m³. The laboratory uses this volume to report a count per cubic metre.

questions.questionText: What do you check about a laboratory before sending samples?
options: It returns results within one day
It is the cheapest laboratory nearby
Its accreditation scope covers the test
It will agree with your hypothesis
questions.explanation: NATA (Australia) and IANZ (New Zealand) accredit laboratories for specific activities. Confirm the test you need is inside the laboratory's scope.

questions.questionText: Which gap makes a sample result hardest to rely on?
options: The cassettes were a new brand
The report arrived on a Friday
No record of the collection location
A courier arrived later than planned
questions.explanation: A result that cannot be tied to a place and time cannot support a decision. Location, time and every hand-over belong on the chain-of-custody form.

questions.questionText: Four air samples cost AUD 85 each and two tape lifts AUD 45 each, ex GST. What is the total inc GST?
options: AUD 430 including GST
AUD 516 including GST
AUD 387 including GST
AUD 473 including GST
questions.explanation: 4 × 85 + 2 × 45 = 430 ex GST. GST at 10% is 43, so the total is AUD 473 inc GST.

quizzes.title: CARSI Indoor Environment Assessment Practitioner — Module 5 check

questions.questionText: What is the "safe spore count" for a home?
options: There is no such guideline value
Below the workplace exposure limit value
Below 400 spores per cubic metre
Whatever the outdoor sample reads today
questions.explanation: enHealth says there is no exposure limit or health guideline value for mould. Interpret by comparison with references, outdoors and trends.

questions.questionText: From when do workplace exposure limits (WEL) apply in Australia?
options: From 30 November 2025
From 1 December 2026
From 1 December 2029
From 1 June 2027
questions.explanation: Safe Work Australia: from 1 December 2026, as each jurisdiction implements it in its WHS laws. Benzene and some state transitions have their own dates.

questions.questionText: What is the benzene WEL from 1 June 2027?
options: 1 ppm 8-hour TWA
0.2 ppm 8-hour TWA
3.2 ppm 8-hour TWA
0.7 ppm 8-hour TWA
questions.explanation: From 1 June 2027 benzene is 0.2 ppm (0.7 mg/m³) 8-hour TWA; until then 1 ppm (3.2 mg/m³) continues. Quote the published pair with source and date.

questions.questionText: A renovator says a solvent level is "fine because it is under the WEL". What is wrong?
options: Nothing, a WEL proves the home safe
A WEL is not a home threshold
The WEL is for mould spores only
The WEL only applies from 2029 onward
questions.explanation: Workplace limits are set for fit adult workers and do not divide healthy from unhealthy. They are never a residential safe-occupancy or clearance threshold.

questions.questionText: How are New Zealand WES described by WorkSafe?
options: As guidance values, not prescribed standards
As identical to the Australian WEL
As limits untrained people should use
As mandatory limits for every home
questions.explanation: WorkSafe NZ says WES and BEI are guidance values, not prescribed exposure standards, and does not recommend untrained people use them to assess risk.

questions.questionText: What must a source tag on a regulatory figure include?
options: Only the number and its unit
A link to some online forums
The assessor name and phone number
Jurisdiction, date, units and averaging time
questions.explanation: Jurisdiction, the date it applies from, units and averaging time, plus a note on what the figure is not (for example, not a residential threshold).

quizzes.title: CARSI Indoor Environment Assessment Practitioner — Module 6 check

questions.questionText: Your personal CO monitor alarms in a room with an unflued gas heater. What first?
options: Finish the readings, then leave the room
Open one window and keep working on
Stop and get everyone into fresh air
Take an air sample for the laboratory
questions.explanation: CO has no smell or taste. Stop, turn off the appliance only if safe, get everyone into fresh air, and call 000 (AU) or 111 (NZ) if anyone is unwell.

questions.questionText: You find a cracked ceiling sheet in a 1975 house. What do you do?
options: Break a piece off to sample
Treat as suspect, do not disturb
Proceed because the crack is small
Look closely to decide by eye
questions.explanation: You cannot tell asbestos by looking. Do not disturb suspect material at any size; record it and refer to a licensed asbestos assessor or competent person.

questions.questionText: According to WorkSafe NZ, which New Zealand buildings could contain asbestos?
options: Any built or renovated before 2000
Only those built before about 2016
Only those built before about 1984
Only those built before about 1990
questions.explanation: WorkSafe NZ says any building built or renovated before 2000 could contain asbestos. In Australia, asbestos was banned in December 2003.

questions.questionText: Someone is sanding a brick wall "to see if it is damp inside". Why stop it?
options: It voids the building insurance policy
It wears out the meter pins
It changes the room dew point
It creates respirable crystalline silica dust
questions.explanation: Cutting, grinding, drilling or sanding brick, concrete or stone creates RCS dust. Choose a non-destructive method or leave it to someone with controls.

questions.questionText: An occupant asks whether the mould caused her child's cough. What do you say?
options: Rule out mould as the cause
Take a sample to find out
Confirm the mould caused the cough
Recommend she talks to her doctor
questions.explanation: Assessors do not diagnose. Public health guidance directs people with symptoms to seek medical advice; record what was reported and recommend that.

questions.questionText: Who is the right referral for exposure monitoring against a workplace limit?
options: The owner or the tenant
The insurer or loss adjuster
An occupational hygienist or IEP
The plumber or the electrician
questions.explanation: Exposure monitoring and interpretation need a competent person such as an occupational hygienist or other indoor environmental professional (IEP).

quizzes.title: CARSI Indoor Environment Assessment Practitioner — Final designation exam

questions.questionText: What comes first in an indoor environment assessment?
options: A thermal camera room sweep
The written question and scope
A full set of samples
A laboratory booking for results
questions.explanation: The written question and scope come first: who commissioned it, the decision it supports and what is excluded. Every reading is planned from it.

questions.questionText: Which of these is a building question an assessment can answer?
options: Is the air safe for babies?
Where is the moisture coming from?
Is the family dog unwell now?
Did mould cause this asthma attack?
questions.explanation: Assessments describe buildings. Health and animal-health questions go to a doctor or vet; mould test results cannot decide health risk.

questions.questionText: In source-pathway-receptor terms, what removes the exposure?
options: Naming the receptor in the report
Measuring every link many more times
Breaking any one of the links
Sampling only at the receptor location
questions.explanation: Exposure needs all three links. Break the source, the pathway or the contact with the receptor and the exposure changes.

questions.questionText: What is usually the root source when mould is the concern?
options: Poor cleaning by the occupants
Old paint on window frames
Outdoor spores blowing in daily
Moisture on surfaces or air
questions.explanation: Mould only grows with enough moisture, and the way to control it is to control the moisture source. Your first hypotheses are about water.

questions.questionText: How many NCC climate zones are there in Australia?
options: Twelve climate zones
Eight climate zones
Four climate zones
Six climate zones
questions.explanation: The NCC groups locations with similar climates into 8 climate zones, used mainly for energy efficiency and condensation management requirements.

questions.questionText: Why compare rooms by g/kg rather than %RH?
options: g/kg is easier for clients to read
RH changes with the air temperature too
g/kg is just the dew point again
RH is only used outdoors in Australia
questions.explanation: RH is not a measure of the actual moisture because it depends on temperature. The humidity ratio (g/kg) compares rooms at different temperatures.

questions.questionText: A surface is below the room dew point. What happens?
options: Nothing until the RH reaches 100%
Condensation forms on that cold surface
The room air becomes drier quickly
The surface warms to room temperature
questions.explanation: Any surface at or below the dew point collects condensation, whatever the room RH reads.

questions.questionText: What makes a moisture meter reading defensible?
options: A single reading per whole room
A reading from a different building
A round number such as ten
A reference from the same material
questions.explanation: Compare like with like: same material, same instrument and mode, against an unaffected reference in the same building, with location and time.

questions.questionText: The NCC F6V1 850 ppm CO2 figure is based on what?
options: An outdoor level of 850 ppm
A 450 ppm rise over 400
A health limit for young children
The Australian workplace limit for CO2
questions.explanation: The ABCB handbook explains it as a 450 ppm rise above an assumed 400 ppm ambient level, an odour and ventilation measure, not a health limit.

questions.questionText: An ATP swab shows a low reading after cleaning. What can you say?
options: The surface is now fully sterile
No mould can be on it
Less organic residue remains on it
The room air is safe now
questions.explanation: ATP is a general cleanliness measure. A low reading shows less organic residue; it is not a mould test or a sterility test.

questions.questionText: What does enHealth say about mould testing in homes generally?
options: It does not recommend testing generally
It requires testing before any sale
It recommends ATP for mould testing
It sets a safe spore count
questions.explanation: enHealth does not recommend testing for mould in general, because there are no health guideline values to compare results with.

questions.questionText: Which body accredits testing laboratories in New Zealand?
options: ABCB in New Zealand
NATA in New Zealand
IANZ in New Zealand
AIOH in New Zealand
questions.explanation: International Accreditation New Zealand (IANZ). In Australia it is NATA. Check that the test you need is in the laboratory's scope.

questions.questionText: What closes the chain of custody for a sample?
options: The courier delivery notice email
The laboratory signed receipt record
The client paying the invoice
The photo taken on site
questions.explanation: Every hand-over is signed and timed, and the laboratory's receipt closes the chain. Photos and IDs tie the sample back to the place it came from.

questions.questionText: Until when do Queensland and Victoria each have a 15-substance WEL transition?
options: Until 30 November 2026
Until 1 December 2029
Until 1 December 2026
Until 1 June 2027
questions.explanation: WorkSafe Queensland and WorkSafe Victoria each set transition arrangements for 15 substances until 1 December 2029.

questions.questionText: Why is a workplace exposure limit never a home clearance threshold?
options: It is set for fit adult workers
It is set by the home insurer
It only applies to the building trade
It is always higher than outdoor air
questions.explanation: Workplace limits are set for fit adult workers over a working week and do not divide healthy from unhealthy. Homes include children and vulnerable people.

questions.questionText: What is the Australian 8-hour standard for respirable crystalline silica?
options: 0.05 mg/m³ 8-hour TWA
0.025 mg/m³ 8-hour TWA
5 mg/m³ 8-hour TWA
0.5 mg/m³ 8-hour TWA
questions.explanation: Safe Work Australia: 0.05 mg/m³ 8-hour TWA, carried into the WEL list at the same value from 1 December 2026. New Zealand's standard is 0.025 mg/m³.

questions.questionText: Carbon monoxide can be detected by which human sense?
options: Taste, as a metal tang
Sight, as a faint haze
None of the human senses
Smell, as a sweet odour
questions.explanation: CO is invisible and has no smell or taste. Only an instrument detects it, which is why a personal monitor alarm is a stop trigger.

questions.questionText: In New Zealand, which section of HSWA 2015 holds the PCBU primary duty of care?
options: Section 56 of HSWA
Section 19 of HSWA
Section 36 of HSWA
Section 23 of HSWA
questions.explanation: HSWA 2015 section 36: a PCBU must ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health and safety of workers and others.

questions.questionText: Which word needs the most support before it goes in a home report?
options: Metres, as a unit measure
Reference, as in a reading
Moisture, as in a finding
Safe, as a health verdict
questions.explanation: Words such as "safe", "toxic" or "clear" need the scope, method and competency behind them; for a home they almost never have it.

questions.questionText: The tenant, landlord and insurer each want a different conclusion. What do you give them?
options: A different version for each one
The same facts in plain words
Only facts that suit the payer
No report until they all agree
questions.explanation: Everyone gets the same facts; only the language changes. State who commissioned the report, and go back to the readings when readers disagree.

quizzes.title: CARSI Indoor Environment Assessment Practitioner — Case assessment IE-001: bedroom moisture

questions.questionText: IE-001 (Hobart bedroom, July). You see dark spotting where the ceiling meets the outside wall. How do you record it in the observation column?
options: Toxic mould confirmed by sight alone
Harmful mould species identified by colour
Health hazard confirmed for the infant
Dark spotting at corner, visual only
questions.explanation: An observation records what you saw. Mould can look like a stain, smudge or discolouration and can be many colours, so neither its look nor its colour identifies a species or a health risk (enHealth).

questions.questionText: IE-001. The bedroom reads 17.0 °C and 74 %RH (dew point 12.3 °C). The corner surface reads 10.5 °C and the mid-wall 15.5 °C. What does this measurement support?
options: Condensation can form on corner
Roof leak is now proven
Mould levels exceed safe limits
The room humidity is unsafe
questions.explanation: The corner surface is below the room's dew point, so water vapour can condense on it; the mid-wall is above it. That supports the condensation hypothesis. It proves no leak and sets no health limit.

questions.questionText: IE-001. The landlord asks for the humidity or spore number above which the bedroom becomes unsafe for the baby. What do you tell him?
options: Seventy per cent RH is unsafe
Use a workplace limit as threshold
There is no universal safe number
Spore counts above 500 mean unsafe
questions.explanation: There is no exposure limit or health guideline value for mould (enHealth). Humidity is a building condition you compare with dew point and surfaces; health questions go to a doctor.

questions.questionText: IE-001. It has been dry for five days, yet the corner is damp every morning and dry by mid-afternoon. Which cause does this weaken most?
options: Overnight condensation on cold surface
Rainwater leaking from roof gutters
Moisture from sleeping occupants overnight
The missing insulation at eave
questions.explanation: A liquid-water leak tracks rain; dampness that comes and goes with the night and the cold surface tracks condensation. The pattern weakens the leak hypothesis without ruling it out for good.

questions.questionText: IE-001. You run the adjoining shower for 10 minutes and re-read the shared wall: no change from the reference. What do you record?
options: Plumbing completely ruled out forever
Shower leak not supported today
Shower leak confirmed by test
Wall is safe to occupy
questions.explanation: One negative test narrows the hypothesis for that test only. Record the method, time and readings; a slow or intermittent leak can still need a licensed plumber later.

questions.questionText: IE-001. Your fourth 'why' finds two adults and an infant sleeping with door and window shut, and clothes drying on an airer. What is the fifth 'why' looking for?
options: Why moisture is not being removed
Who is to blame for mould
Which mould species is growing there
Whether the tenant should be evicted
questions.explanation: The Five Whys ends at a cause someone can fix, not at blame. Here: no ventilation habit, no exhaust and a window kept shut. enHealth says opening a door or window is the cheapest way to reduce indoor moisture.

questions.questionText: IE-001. From the manhole you see the ceiling insulation pulled back at the eave above the corner. Who puts it right?
options: The assessor, during the visit
An occupational hygienist, after sampling
The tenant's doctor, by referral
A builder or insulation installer
questions.explanation: Fixing building fabric is trade work. The assessor records it from the manhole and does not enter or work in the roof space, which may hold cabling and, in older houses, asbestos.

questions.questionText: IE-001. The parent says the baby has had a cough for two weeks. What goes in your report?
options: The mould is causing the cough
Cough confirms mould exposure in bedroom
Recorded as reported; refer to doctor
The cough rules out condensation entirely
questions.explanation: Symptoms are recorded as reported and never diagnosed. enHealth: if you are concerned about symptoms, seek medical advice.

questions.questionText: IE-001, New Zealand version: the same house is a Dunedin rental. Which NZ rule speaks directly to the bedroom?
options: Healthy homes ventilation standard for rentals
Australian NCC climate zone seven rules
WorkSafe NZ workplace exposure standards apply
No rule covers rental home ventilation
questions.explanation: Under the healthy homes ventilation standard, openable windows, doors and skylights in each room of a rental must together be at least 5% of its floor area (Tenancy Services).

quizzes.lessonTitle: Case assessment IE-002: floodwater with pets
quizzes.title: CARSI Indoor Environment Assessment Practitioner — Case assessment IE-002: floodwater with pets

questions.questionText: IE-002 (Ipswich house, day 2 after floodwater reached 320 mm). No mould is visible and there is no musty smell. What do you record about mould?
options: Present, because every flood means mould
Not observed today; later risk noted
Confirmed by smell of the floodwater
Present; take spore samples to confirm
questions.explanation: Record only what you observed. Wet furniture and surfaces get mouldy after a couple of days (NZ Civil Defence), so mould is a developing risk to note and manage by drying, not a finding to assume.

questions.questionText: IE-002. Do you sample the floodwater to decide whether it is contaminated?
options: Yes, before anyone wears gloves
Yes, results decide the PPE
Only if sewage smell present
No, presume it is contaminated
questions.explanation: Floodwater is often contaminated by sewage and agricultural or industrial wastes (Queensland Government), so it is treated as contaminated. A sample would answer no decision question.

questions.questionText: IE-002. The owner wants to switch the power back on to run fans. What do you say?
options: Not until a licensed electrician checks
Yes, if the safety switch holds
Yes, the floor has now dried
Only the circuits above water level
questions.explanation: After flood damage a licensed electrician carries out verification tests before supply is reconnected (Electrical Safety Office Queensland). Stay away from a water-damaged switchboard.

questions.questionText: IE-002. One dog drank floodwater and is now lethargic. What is your role?
options: Diagnose leptospirosis from the dog's symptoms
Advise antibiotics from the first-aid kit
Record it; owner contacts vet now
Wait until the house is dry
questions.explanation: Animal health belongs to a vet. Leptospirosis affects people and animals and spreads more easily after floods (Queensland Government); a lethargic dog should see a vet promptly. You record a non-clinical concern only.

questions.questionText: IE-002. A fibre-cement eave lining on the 1960s house has been broken by debris. What do you do?
options: Treat as suspect; do not disturb
Sweep it up with the silt
Snap off a sample to test
Water-blast it clean, then inspect it
questions.explanation: You cannot tell asbestos by looking, and damaged non-friable asbestos can release fibres (Safe Work Australia). Keep people away and refer to a licensed asbestos assessor or competent person.

questions.questionText: IE-002. The kitchen smells strongly. Which is a plausible competing cause to the sewage hypothesis?
options: Carbon dioxide from the occupants' breath
Radio signals from the meter box
Food spoiling in an unpowered fridge
The relative humidity reading on screen
questions.explanation: Good hypotheses are physically possible and testable. Spoiled food in a fridge without power is a real odour source to check before blaming sewage; carbon dioxide has no smell.

questions.questionText: IE-002. Indoors reads 27 °C and 85 %RH (19.1 g/kg); outdoors 29 °C and 78 %RH (19.7 g/kg). What does this tell you?
options: Indoor air is unsafe to breathe
Outdoor air is far drier today
Mould will grow within one hour
Opening up removes little moisture today
questions.explanation: Outdoor air holds as much water per kilogram as indoor air, so natural ventilation carries little moisture out that day. It is a drying decision, not a health verdict.

questions.questionText: IE-002. The back stairs move underfoot and part of the deck has dropped. What happens?
options: Test it by jumping on it
Keep off; refer to structural engineer
Prop it with a dehumidifier box
Note it only if it's insured
questions.explanation: Structural adequacy is outside assessor competency. Exclude people from the area and refer to a builder or structural engineer before anyone uses it.

questions.questionText: IE-002, New Zealand version: a flooded Gisborne house. What does Health New Zealand say about floodwater?
options: Safe once it looks clear again
Test before deciding on any PPE
Assume contaminated with sewage and chemicals
Only farm floodwater carries any risk
questions.explanation: Health NZ: always assume floodwater is contaminated with farm run-off, animal and human sewage and chemicals. Health questions go to a doctor or Healthline 0800 611 116.

quizzes.lessonTitle: Case assessment IE-003: renovation, VOCs and HVAC
quizzes.title: CARSI Indoor Environment Assessment Practitioner — Case assessment IE-003: renovation, VOCs and HVAC

questions.questionText: IE-003 (Melbourne townhouse, new kitchen). Heater off. A TVOC indicator reads 2.1 in the kitchen and 0.1 outdoors; the personal CO monitor reads 0 ppm. What do you record?
options: VOC indicator raised; CO not detected
Carbon monoxide confirmed by chemical odour
VOC reading proves the heater leaks
Air is unsafe above workplace limit
questions.explanation: Record each reading as it is. A raised VOC indicator says nothing about carbon monoxide, and 0 ppm with the heater off says nothing about the heater in use. CO has no smell (WorkSafe NZ).

questions.questionText: IE-003. The occupant says: 'There's no smell when the heater runs, so there can't be CO.' What do you reply?
options: Correct, no smell means no CO
A VOC meter will detect CO
CO has no smell; refer gasfitter
Open a window and stop worrying
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide is invisible and has no smell or taste; other combustion gases may smell, but an odour can neither confirm nor exclude CO. A gasfitter checks the heater.

questions.questionText: IE-003. Headaches are worse in the evening when the open-flued heater, rangehood and bathroom fan all run. Which hypothesis does this raise?
options: Particleboard producing carbon monoxide at night
Exhaust fans drawing flue gases indoors
The CO monitor being too sensitive
Humidity alone causing the evening headaches
questions.explanation: Energy Safe Victoria: with an exhaust fan running and too little ventilation, negative pressure can draw carbon monoxide into living spaces through the heater's flue. It is a hypothesis for a gasfitter to test.

questions.questionText: IE-003. Do you run the heater with every fan on to test for spillage yourself?
options: Yes, for thirty minutes, windows shut
Yes, if the monitor is calibrated
Yes, with the doors left open
No; a licensed gasfitter tests it
questions.explanation: Negative-pressure and spillage testing is gas service work, guided for gasfitters by Energy Safe Victoria. Creating a possible CO exposure to test a hypothesis is never part of an assessment.

questions.questionText: IE-003. Until the gasfitter attends, what interim advice do you pass on from Energy Safe Victoria?
options: Run every fan to clear the air
Seal the vents to keep warmth in
Use the heater only at night time
Do not run exhaust fans with heater
questions.explanation: Energy Safe Victoria: don't operate exhaust fans at the same time as your heater. If anyone is unwell, get into fresh air and call 000 (Australia) or 111 (New Zealand).

questions.questionText: IE-003. The owner asks whether the kitchen VOC reading is under 'the safe limit' in the workplace list. What do you answer?
options: Yes, below the WEL means safe
Workplace limits are not home thresholds
Yes, compare with the benzene limit
No, any reading above zero harms
questions.explanation: Workplace limits are set for workers and are not even a dividing line at work (Safe Work Australia). Home readings are compared with outdoors and unaffected rooms, and ventilation follows YourHome advice.

questions.questionText: IE-003, occupational extension. In May 2027 the contractor's workers are on a site where benzene is a listed airborne contaminant. Which Australian limit applies?
options: 1 ppm (3.2 mg/m³) 8-hour TWA
0.2 ppm (0.7 mg/m³) 8-hour TWA
No benzene limit applies until 2029
The home TVOC reading applies instead
questions.explanation: Safe Work Australia (29/10/2026): until 1 June 2027 the benzene limit stays at 1 ppm (3.2 mg/m³) 8-hour TWA, workplace only, subject to each jurisdiction's WHS laws.

questions.questionText: IE-003, occupational extension. The same contractor starts a job on 15 June 2027. Which Australian benzene limit applies?
options: 1 ppm (3.2 mg/m³) 8-hour TWA
The 2025 WES value still applies
0.2 ppm (0.7 mg/m³) 8-hour TWA
The residential reading sets the limit
questions.explanation: From 1 June 2027 the WEL for benzene falls to 0.2 ppm (0.7 mg/m³) 8-hour TWA (Safe Work Australia). Check implementation with the state or territory WHS regulator; it is never a household figure.

questions.questionText: IE-003, New Zealand version: a Wellington house where the flued gas heater shows soot and a yellow flame. What does WorkSafe NZ say?
options: Keep it running to burn soot off
Turn it off; call licensed gas worker
Yellow flames are always a normal feature
Clean the flue yourself, then relight it
questions.explanation: WorkSafe NZ: a yellow flame, soot or a car-exhaust smell are warning signs; turn the appliance off and contact a licensed gas worker immediately.

quizzes.lessonTitle: Case assessment IE-004: commercial renovation dust
quizzes.title: CARSI Indoor Environment Assessment Practitioner — Case assessment IE-004: commercial renovation dust

questions.questionText: IE-004 (Toowoomba, March 2027). Contractors are cutting fibre-cement sheet in a 1978 tenancy and no asbestos register is on site. What do you do?
options: Collect the offcuts for lab testing
Ask them to wet it down
Stop that work; refer licensed assessor
Continue; bonded sheet is always safe
questions.explanation: Asbestos was banned in Australia in December 2003, you cannot tell it by looking, and businesses working with it must keep an asbestos register (Safe Work Australia). Stop, keep people away and refer.

questions.questionText: IE-004. The sheet is confirmed as non-friable asbestos and 14.4 m² must come out. In Queensland, who removes it?
options: The shopfitter, as it is bonded
A Class A or B removalist
Anyone wearing a P2 face mask
The property manager's own cleaning crew
questions.explanation: WorkSafe Queensland: a class B licence covers removal of more than 10 m² of non-friable asbestos, and class A holders may also do class B work.

questions.questionText: IE-004. In Queensland in March 2027, which limit applies to softwood dust for the framing crew?
options: The new WEL applied from December 2026
No limit at all applies to it
The pharmacy particle count sets the limit
The WES continues until 1 December 2029
questions.explanation: Softwood dust is one of Queensland's 15 transition substances: the WES continues to apply until 1 December 2029 (WorkSafe Queensland). The PCBU must still minimise exposure so far as is reasonably practicable.

questions.questionText: IE-004. A diesel forklift runs in the loading dock. In Queensland in 2027, what applies to diesel particulate matter?
options: Interim 0.1 mg/m³ TWA until 2029
No limit until 1 December 2029
The national WEL from December 2026
The shop's PM2.5 reading sets it
questions.explanation: WorkSafe Queensland: for DPM measured as respirable elemental carbon, a TWA of 0.1 mg/m³ applies until 1 December 2029. 'No limit' is the flour-dust arrangement, not DPM.

questions.questionText: IE-004. In May 2027 a labourer mixes Portland cement for a slab patch on the Queensland site. Which list applies?
options: The new WEL, since December 2026
No list; cement is not covered
Victoria's list, being the stricter one
The existing WES, until December 2029
questions.explanation: Portland cement is a Queensland transition substance, so the WES continues until 1 December 2029. Victoria has its own 15-substance transition; never flatten the dates into one national rule.

questions.questionText: IE-004. The pharmacy manager asks whether the shop is 'clear' because silica is under 0.05 mg/m³. What do you answer?
options: A workplace limit is not clearance
Yes, below 0.05 means customers safe
Yes, if the reading was 8-hour
No, it must be 0.025 instead
questions.explanation: 0.05 mg/m³ 8-hour TWA is the Australian workplace exposure standard for workers' breathing zones (Safe Work Australia). It is not a customer, household or clearance level.

questions.questionText: IE-004. Particle counts in the pharmacy rise when the grinder runs while outdoor counts stay steady, and the shared ceiling void above the hoarding is unsealed. Which pathway fits best?
options: From the street, through the doors
Through the open shared ceiling void
From the pharmacy's own cardboard stock
From people breathing inside the shop
questions.explanation: The counts track the grinder, not the street, and there is an open path through the ceiling void. A particle counter is an indicator: it shows a pathway, not what the dust is.

questions.questionText: IE-004. Old painted timber window frames are being dry-sanded. What does WorkSafe Queensland say about identifying lead paint?
options: Lead paint is always bright white
A negative swab proves it absent
It cannot be identified by appearance
Only pre-1950 homes ever contain it
questions.explanation: Lead-based paint cannot be identified by its appearance, and test kits can give false results (WorkSafe Queensland). Treat it as possible and refer to the PCBU and an occupational hygienist.

questions.questionText: IE-004, New Zealand version: the tenancy is in Hamilton. Which NZ position on non-friable asbestos removal is right?
options: More than 10 m² needs a licence
Any amount can go without a licence
Only friable asbestos is ever licensed work
Australian state rules apply in New Zealand
questions.explanation: WorkSafe NZ: up to and including 10 m² of non-friable asbestos over the whole project needs no licence; more needs a Class A or Class B removalist.
